subject.title: Cron jobs stall during AI model calls (model_call:stream_progress never completes)

question: Should the remaining work stay on this issue as the cron wake-now result contract, or should maintainers split that into a new focused issue and close this one after the model-call stall ships?
rationale: Current main fixes the headline stream-progress hang, but the issue discussion and source still show a separate wake-now result semantics gap; automation should not choose the tracking or API contract shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Split wake-now contract
options.body: Open or designate a focused issue for wake-now success/failure semantics, then close this issue after the model-call stall fix is release-proven.

options.title: Keep scoped here
options.body: Keep this issue open but retitle/scope it to the wake-now result contract so the fixed stream-progress path does not confuse triage.

options.title: Accept fire-and-forget wake
options.body: Document that cron.wake reports enqueue success only and ask for a fresh report if a concrete heartbeat failure remains after the next release.

recommendation.title: Split wake-now contract
recommendation.body: Open or designate a focused issue for wake-now success/failure semantics, then close this issue after the model-call stall fix is release-proven.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the reliability stack and already posted the current scoping guidance on this issue.
